- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.16) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or align with 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.23) mid-horizon, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–5% relative to prior 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates downward moves in 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative — add 1–3% buffer to forecast for negative sentiment periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per 3-day lag; if below, increase by 1–2% per 3-day lag.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–2 days in downward moves — adjust down by 0.5–1.5% for each day of lag in negative sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast with 5-day moving average before final output.
